The Next Evolution of AI Is Learning From Your Dodgy Gaming Skills
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
09:00:00 UTC
18:00:00 KST

With the twirl of a thumbstick, squeeze of a trigger, and press of a few buttons, even an unskilled player can dance their way through a 3D video game environment. A British startup is wagering that straightforward sequences like these contain a trove of information that can be used to train new artificial intelligence models.
There is a growing belief in corners of the AI industry that large language models will ultimately be limited by their inability to navigate the physical world. Trained only on words, LLMs are perhaps ill-equipped to pilot autonomous vehicles, steer robotic arms, or perform any other action that requires finesse and precision. To remedy that shortcoming, a crop of celebrated researchers including Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun are focusing their efforts on a different class of AI: world models.
To become fluent in real-world physics, world models need to be trained on a combination of visual and action data. Before it can deftly maneuver a robotic arm, a model might need to be trained on video footage of the factory floor, coupled with information about how firmly an object should be gripped, with what torque it’s manipulated, and so on. But unlike LLMs, trained on oceans of text, there is no similar corpus of material available to world model labs.
“For world models, you need cause and consequence,” says Xiatian Zhu, an associate professor specializing in AI at the University of Surrey. “On the internet, we have very little of this type of data.”
Worldmodeldata, a British startup advised by LeCun, is aiming to solve that problem by packaging controller inputs and other data collected by video game studios—an exhaust product available in massive quantities—into training datasets for world models. Some companies, like General Intuition and Niantic, are already collecting video game data from their own platforms to build models. But Worldmodeldata pitches itself as a broker that curates and organizes data, saving labs from striking individual agreements with tons of game studios.
“There are millions of great games, and they are more and more similar to the real world,” Rhea Loucas, CEO of Worldmodeldata, tells WIRED. “Why don’t we take the vast, abundant, diverse experiences from video games, and teach AI?”
Though the hypothesis is yet to be fully tested, researchers are broadly working under the assumption that the performance of world models will improve in line with the size of their training datasets, in a similar way to LLMs. That means the shortage of suitable training data is one of the largest bottlenecks to progress.
Some labs have tried to manually generate their own data by attaching sensors to humans and robots in testing environments. But that approach yields only a small amount of data, and it doesn’t account for the fringe scenarios a model might encounter in the wild.
“You can pay people to demonstrate pick-and-place tasks. But repetition alone won’t capture the disorder of the world you’re asking a machine to operate in,” says Nicole Fraenkel, a partner at VC firm Khosla Ventures, which has invested in General Intuition.
Worldmodeldata’s theory is that data collected from video game environments—visual representations of a 3D space paired with actions taken by the player—is both available in the necessary quantities and sufficiently varied to capture all-important corner cases.
“The corner cases are the ones to actually get right,” says Fraenkel. “The cost of error with a car, plane, drone, factory forklift, or autonomous quadruped is very high.”
Worldmodeldata says it has licensed almost 1 million hours' worth of data from studios behind various popular video games, though Loucas declined to name them. In the future, the startup is aiming to create avenues for individual players to be compensated, too.
Loucas believes that video game data will ultimately make up the majority of the training material for world models, which will later be optimized using data specific to a given real-world environment or task. “This could well lead to the GPT moment for world models—making them really useful,” Loucas claims.
Not everybody shares the same optimism about video game data, though. Nvidia, which publishes a family of world models optimized to run on its chips, prefers to use a custom engine it devised specifically to replicate real-world physics as the backbone for its AI.
Ming-Yu Liu, who leads world model development at Nvidia, says that models trained on video game inputs are unlikely to fare well with tasks that require fine-grained motor control, like the careful manipulation of objects. That’s because video game physics is often eccentric, and developers take shortcuts to create the illusion of realism—a character dips a hand to collect an apple from the table—without coding in the details: the pressure applied by each finger to prevent the apple slipping from their grasp.
“I would be more conservative on using video game data for manipulation,” Liu says. “The physics for manipulation is much more involved.” Training on video game data is better reserved, he says, for world models meant for generating hyperrealistic video or 3D environments.
Zhu, the academic from the University of Surrey, has similar concerns. “Video games are, in essence, simulators. They do have some degree of physical grounding,” he says. “But they are very coarse, approximate.”
But until world models reach their ChatGPT moment, all kinds of ideas for getting them there remain on the table. “There are many paths to the promised land,” says Fraenkel. “The truth is, the jury is still out on which one is going to work best.”

Nvidia’s Answer to Rogue Agents Is an Open-Source AI Security System
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
09:00:00 UTC
18:00:00 KST

Amidst ongoing reports of AI agents wreaking havoc on online infrastructure, chipmaker Nvidia is rallying tech companies to use its new open-source tool for AI security.
Over the last few months, frontier AI labs have disclosed multiple incidents in which AI agents have hacked into other companies or, in more recent examples, probed official US and Australian government websites. While Nvidia has already taken a leading role in rallying the AI industry around open source security, it’s now introducing one new software security platform and making an agentic AI sandbox more broadly available.
OpenShell, one of the Nvidia’s recently launched security sandboxes for AI agents, is now entering general release for all users. OpenShell was first announced at Nvidia’s annual GTC Conference in March; it’s a framework for containing agents as they carry out tasks and isolating their activity in the operating system kernel, the foundational program that has access to virtually all parts of a computer system in order to coordinate hardware and software.
Nvidia’s launch materials indicate that it has AI safety and security collaborations with dozens of other tech companies, including Anthropic, Cisco, CoreWeave, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, Hugging Face, JPMorganChase, Mistral, Microsoft, and Palantir. Nvidia says SpaceXAI is using the Open Agent Safety Platform for its Cursor agents and Grok models. The company also says Anthropic and Nvidia are “building security into Claude Managed Agents.” Salesforce, Scale AI, and SAP are all confirmed to be integrating OpenShell to some degree. However, it is unclear whether OpenShell has been adopted by Nvidia’s full list of partners, or whether Nvidia is gesturing broadly.
One notable name is missing entirely from Nvidia’s list: OpenAI. Both companies indicated that OpenAI is a part of Nvidia’s OpenShell effort, though both declined to comment directly on why the AI lab was excluded from the announcement.
Security engineers and AI safety experts have considered the need to isolate and monitor agentic AI since well before the recent revelations of rogue agent hacking. Nvidia’s own OpenShell announcement in March noted that the framework would add “privacy and security controls to make self-evolving, autonomous AI agents, or claws, more trustworthy, scalable and accessible,” months before OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents had hacked the open source AI company Hugging Face. (Nvidia agreed to acquire Hugging Face earlier this month for $12.9 billion.)
The chip giant has also developed a new software platform called Sentry, an isolated security domain for chips that’s supposed to continuously monitor long-running AI agents. While Sentry is technically a software tool, it’s meant to be implemented on Bluefield, Nvidia’s line of programmable data processing units (DPUs). The idea is that in addition to the restrictions imposed by OpenShell, Sentry can act as a separate, independent mechanism that can “quarantine agents that attempt to move outside their boundaries.”
Sentry is another way for Nvidia customers and open-source users to actually implement security policies through OpenShell, says Justin Boitano, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of enterprise computing. While traditional sandboxes are built for “application-level isolation,” people now want to run fleets of agents, which demands a “collective policy across all of those agents,” he says.
“Agents are very creative at finding ways to achieve the goals that they’re given,” Boitano says. “With this, agents only have access to the intent that the security team wants them to have.”
Boitano adds that Nvidia is working with both Arm and Intel to create a version of Sentry that works on the x86 chip architecture. “Once it runs on those instruction-set architectures, it can run on any architecture,” he says.
Nvidia is positioning all of this as part of a new open-source framework called the Open Agent Safety Platform, which now encompasses OpenShell and Sentry as well.
In July Nvidia launched an industry-wide AI safety coalition that now comprises more than 120 companies. The coalition’s stated goal was to reduce AI risks, particularly through a program called the Shared AI Findings Exchange (SAFE). Last month, Boitano said that SAFE was designed to be “governed independently, with no single company or industry segment controlling its findings.”
But one company keeps appearing at the center of these industry-wide, open-source AI initiatives, and that company is Nvidia. The world’s most valuable company, on which most of the tech industry depends on for the most performant chips, appears to be positioning itself to deepen its influence and set standards at varying levels of the AI technology stack, from silicon to security software.
Though efforts to contain and control agents are already in progress throughout the industry, recent rogue agent behavior suggests a need to raise awareness about long-standing, core security practices—even, apparently, within trillion-dollar frontier labs. Some experts say that this also gets to the heart of the question about what it really means for an autonomous piece of software to “go rogue.”
“Anything that makes it easy for companies to deploy agents in a way that has more guardrails and more safety should be applauded,” says longtime security engineer and researcher Niels Provos, speaking generally about tools geared toward containing and monitoring agents. Provos himself launched an open source framework in February focused on these issues. “If nothing else, these types of tools help to dispel the myth that agents can’t be controlled.”

Twelve Countries Oppose French Push for EU Defence Preference
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:57:08 UTC
17:57:08 KST

Twelve countries are pushing to keep the bloc’s future defence programmes open to military allies outside the EU, challenging France’s drive for strict European preference rules.
A non-paper, signed by Germany, Austria, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Italy, Latvia, the Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Sweden and Slovenia, pushes back against a French drive for strict European preference in the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), a key part of the next EU budget.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Openness for participation of third countries is a very important signal to our allies and partners outside the EU,” the paper said.
European capitals face tough negotiations over the EU’s next long-term budget for 2028-2034, with distinct priorities on competitiveness, defence and security. Third countries are non-EU states.
“We must cooperate closely to ensure our defence readiness, specifically the interoperability and standardisation of our military equipment,” the 12 countries said.
“Associations can leverage the impact of EU funding by increasing funding budgets, economies of scale as well as efficiencies, resilience and innovation along supply chains,” the paper added, pointing to a need for flexibility in light of the changing security environment.
The paper further argues that the EU “should retain the automatic participation of EEA countries and Ukraine in the defence industry section without an association agreement”.
EU Agrees to Release €6.6B for Ukraine From EPF, Once Blocked by Orbán
The European Commission’s proposed €2 trillion budget would include over €409 billion for the European Competitiveness Fund – including €175 billion from the research and innovation programme Horizon. The EU executive foresees €130 billion for defence and space, though the exact split is unclear.
However, the competitiveness fund is unlikely to remain intact at that level. A previous draft had already proposed cuts of around 4%, compared to the EU executive’s blueprint.
France, by contrast, wants strict European preference rules in the future budget and sees them as a core objective.
“As for European funds, they must be used to reduce our dependencies by investing jointly to support our innovation ecosystems and our defence and space sectors,” Benjamin Haddad, the French EU affairs minister, said earlier in the summer.
“The eligibility criteria for SAFE [Security Action for Europe] and EDIP [European Defence Industry Programme] … set a good precedent for the European Competitiveness Fund”, he added.
EDIP, worth €1.5 billion, and SAFE, a €150 billion instrument, mandate a minimum of two-thirds European components and protect the design authority.
One diplomat critical of the French position said that “Paris is isolated”.
“France simply cannot afford to stall European defence investments,” the diplomat said. “We must not lose sight of the broader geopolitical landscape. We should be strengthening our strategic defence ties with key partners like Canada or the UK, not compromising them for the sake of domestic industrial interests.”
Another diplomat backed the French position. European preference is the added value of the ECF, which is about EU money, the diplomat argued.
“EDIP is supposed to be the precedent. Every country has decided to increase their national defence budget to meet the NATO spending targets, they can use that money the way they want. Here it’s about EU money.”
Defence industry players have also been calling for “clear European preference” rules, after a recent US non-paper urged European co-legislators to replace “European preference” with a “made with Europe” or “made in NATO” approach.
Washington argued that restrictions proposed for the ECF and already included in the SAFE and EDIP instruments would weaken the transatlantic defence industrial base.
The dispute comes as capitals are rushing to close a deal on the future budget by the end of the year, ahead of elections across the bloc – including the French presidential election in April, which could sweep Marine Le Pen, a far-right Eurosceptic, into the Élysée.

Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines – NBC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:56:59 UTC

Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines – NBC
Eight US Marines were injured when an Iranian anti-ship cruise missile struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz that they were operating on earlier this month, NBC News reported on Sunday, citing sources. The Pentagon has not offered an account of the incident and is facing scrutiny over whether it is downplaying the number of casualties and costs in the war with Iran.
The Marines – seven enlisted personnel and one officer – were operating as part of a landing team when the missile hit, unnamed US officials told the network. The personnel suffered smoke inhalation and possible traumatic brain injuries, but none were seriously wounded, the report claims.
NBC sources said the Marines were not aboard a US Navy ship but did not identify the type of vessel.
The Pentagon did not provide an explanation for the incident. It took it nearly ten days to quietly add the Marines into the Defense Casualty Analysis System, a database that tracks injuries and deaths in the conflict.
Just last week, the tally abruptly rose by 37, bringing the acknowledged number of US troops wounded since the hostilities began to 861, with more than half categorized as casualties of ‘Overseas Operations’ rather than specifying the unpopular war against Iran.
Earlier this month, the Washington Post also reported that at least 22 service members died in the Middle East since the war began, compared with 18 acknowledged by the Pentagon at the time.
While it is unclear whether the Trump administration was deliberately downplaying the toll, or the discrepancy was caused by bureaucratic procedures, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth denounced the report as “DISGUSTING and FAKE.”
The dispute over the human toll has been accompanied by questions over the financial costs of the conflict. CENTCOM estimates the costs of military operations against Iran at around $43.6 billion, but the figure does not include the potential multi-billion-dollar cost of repairing US military facilities hit in retaliatory strikes.
NBC reported in July, citing people familiar with Pentagon assessments, that the overall cost could already be $80 billion to $100 billion when repairing bases, replacing destroyed aircraft, and fully replenishing weapons are included.
Iran has warned that it has “unforgettable lessons” in store for the US if it continues the escalation, saying it will only lead to “heavier costs and further humiliation.” Last week, President Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that Iran “does not seek to kill Americans” but will resist the pressure campaign.

Göktaş's arrest was the latest in a widening crackdown on anyone seen as critical of Turkey's conservative government or its values, which has netted hundreds of politicians, artists, musicians, journalists and LGBTQ+ activists.
A popular Turkish comedian has gone on trial at an Istanbul court on Monday on charges of insulting President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and other offences during a stand-up performance in June.
Deniz Göktaş, a 32-year-old comedian known for his dry wit and political satire, was arrested by police on 3 July, a week after releasing a YouTube video of his show that was watched nearly 9 million times.
Held in pre-trial detention ever since, Göktaş is facing charges of insulting Erdoğan and incitement to public hatred, with prosecutors later adding an extra charge of praising crime and criminals, according to the indictment.
Göktaş's arrest was the latest in a widening crackdown on anyone seen as critical of Turkey's conservative government or its values, which has netted hundreds of politicians, artists, musicians, journalists and LGBTQ+ activists among others.
In the pouring rain, around 50 protesters with umbrellas gathered outside Istanbul's Çağlayan courthouse under the watch of several dozen police, chanting: "Denis Göktaş is not alone!" an AFP correspondent said.
Several dozen police were also inside as a crowd of journalists and supporters waited to enter the courtroom where Göktaş was expected to attend in person.
Among them were several comedians from Istanbul's TuzBiber comedy club where Göktaş reportedly began his career in 2019.
There were also observers from the Dutch embassy and the US consulate.
X posts from jail
The comedian is being held at Karatepe high-security prison, about 120 kilometres west of Istanbul and has been able to give an occasional post on X, mostly wry observations about life behind bars.
"After 88 days, I'll be handcuffed for the first time and hear a car horn. I'm definitely not missing the handcuffs," he posted late Sunday, on the eve of his first day in court.
"A 90-minute show spawns a new charge every two months," he wrote in late August, saying they had added the extra charge against him "for a joke about the Daltons," one of Turkey's organised crime groups.
Although the indictment did not clearly outline the sentence, calculations by the Turkish media suggested that if convicted on all charges, he could face up to a decade or more behind bars, Anka news agency reported, with other outlets giving a similar figure.
According to Turkish media, the Ankara-born comedian began his career at TuzBiber in Istanbul and has gone on to perform at venues across Europe and the US.

Two Israeli siblings airlifted from Nepal village after storm causes landslides, flooding
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:53:09 UTC
17:53:09 KST

Israeli siblings Maya Lamdan, 27, and Nadav Lamdan, 21, were rescued by helicopter on Sunday from the village of Samagaun in Nepal's Manaslu trekking region after hours of anxiety, power outages, and landslides around the village.
The siblings, from Tzur Hadassah, were evacuated to Kathmandu. Their sister, Roni Lamdan, who traveled with them to Nepal, did not take part in the trek and was not in the village when the incident occurred.
Maya, her brother, and their friends were evacuated by PassportCard helicopter to Kathmandu and were undergoing examinations at a hospital. Maya told Walla that she and her brother had gone traveling after completing combat military service.
"Already after a few days of being stuck in the village, we saw that a rain system was approaching, and we stayed there so that we would be somewhere safe rather than continuing the trek. But the last 24 hours were far beyond what we expected."
According to Maya, the travelers spent about 12 hours without electricity or heating as temperatures fell below freezing.
"Toward the evening, the rain continued to intensify. At 3:00 a.m., when we were already asleep, someone knocked on the door of our room. We heard a very loud noise and were told to go up to the roof because a flood was coming."
Only in the morning did they learn it wasn't a flood, but two nearby landslides.
"All the locals started running from the village toward the hills with headlamps. There was real panic, if you can even call them streets. We waited on the roof and tried to understand what was happening. It was dark, and it wasn't clear how close it was. Throughout the day, there were another three or four smaller landslides. We were literally surrounded by this event 360 degrees," she said.
At least 10 additional Israelis were in village during storm
Five Israelis were in the group traveling with Maya, and she said that at least 10 other Israelis were staying in the village at the time.
"At least physically, we're all healthy and safe. Mentally, it will take us a little time to recover. There was an insane sense of helplessness and anxiety that hit some of the people, especially at night," she said.
Lamdan said she knew of other Israelis who remained in the area and had been told that they were also being assisted.
"We were split up during the rescue, but they told us that everyone would be rescued by Monday," she said.
PassportCard's emergency operations center said it had been assisting dozens of Israeli travelers in Nepal in recent hours following severe weather and heavy rainfall.
According to the company, 17 of its insured travelers were in the Annapurna region, 17 in the Manaslu region, including Samagaun, four in the Tsum Valley, and two in the Everest region.
Four of the insured travelers required medical attention and were expected to be evacuated for treatment as soon as weather conditions allowed. The company stressed that none were in life-threatening condition and that their families were in regular contact with the emergency operations center.
The severe weather has severely restricted movement across large parts of Nepal, with many roads blocked and trekking suspended. According to current forecasts, the rain was expected to gradually weaken on Sunday and Monday, although a return to normal conditions in the area could take several days.
Clal rescue teams operating to evacuate insured Israeli travelers
Clal Insurance and Finance said its rescue teams, operating through its rescue company Magen Search and Rescue, were working in the field to evacuate insured Israeli travelers who had encountered extreme weather in Nepal and required assistance.
Clal Insurance and Finance said it was aware of 10 travelers insured by the company. Three had been evacuated to Kathmandu, while seven others were being rescued and were also expected to be transferred to Kathmandu and Pokhara.
"Clal Insurance and Finance is working together with all its rescue teams in Nepal to assist all insured travelers who require rescue. We are in contact with all relevant parties to ensure that the incident ends safely and that all our insured travelers are rescued and transferred to a safe location," said Dror Zasler, deputy CEO and head of claims.

Ukrainians' biggest concerns are corruption and Russian missile and drone attacks – poll
According to a survey, 50% of Ukrainians are currently concerned about corruption in Ukraine, while another 40% are concerned about large-scale missile and drone attacks.
Source: a survey by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS), conducted from 12 to 21 September 2026
Details: Other issues causing the greatest concern include the lack of professionalism and competence among the authorities (30%), low salaries and pensions (28%), the activities of military enlistment offices (24%), rising prices (23%) and the situation on the front line (21%). Other issues were mentioned less frequently.
Sociologists noted that a total of 53% of respondents selected either "large-scale missile and drone attacks" or "the situation on the front line" (or both), meaning that war as a source of concern is on a par with corruption.
In addition, a large majority of respondents – 72% – believe that the level of corruption in the country has increased since the start of the full-scale invasion. Six per cent believe it has decreased. The remainder either believe it has not changed or were unable to answer.
For reference: The KIIS survey was conducted from 12 to 21 September 2026 using telephone interviews in all regions of Ukraine under government control. A total of 1,002 respondents were interviewed. The survey covered adult Ukrainian citizens aged 18 and over who, at the time of the survey, were living in Ukrainian government-controlled territory.
Under normal circumstances, the statistical margin of error for such a sample (with a 0.95 confidence level and taking into account a design effect of 1.3) would not exceed 4.1% for figures close to 50%, 3.5% for figures close to 25%, 2.5% for figures close to 10% and 1.8% for figures close to 5%.
In wartime conditions, a certain degree of systematic bias should be considered in addition to the stated statistical margin of error.

Minister: Trump-Zelenskyy UN encounter did not bring peace any closer

Minister: Trump-Zelenskyy UN encounter did not bring peace any closer
US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's recent meeting did little to advance the Ukraine peace process, Foreign Minister Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said.
The meeting took place last Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly (UNGA), which Tsahkna attended.
The minister noted it focused more on practical issues, such as licensing the production of Patriot systems under license, intelligence and defending Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter.
On the other hand, it did not move things any close to peace, Tsahkna went on, talking to "Ukraina stuudio".
"We have not actually moved any closer to peace, and Zelenskyy was absolutely right when he said in his speech and comments that it seems all the world's leaders want peace, but the only person who does not is Putin. The fact that the meeting with President Trump took place on the sidelines of the UN was good news by itself. I also got the opportunity to meet the Ukrainian foreign minister immediately after he came out of the room. He said it had been more of a practical meeting," Tsahkna said.
"President Zelenskyy has clearly said that they are prepared, if Russia stops bombing their energy infrastructure, to also halt their deep strikes. But in reality, nothing like that happened. And perhaps an even more interesting meeting, about which we know less, was the meeting between [U.S. Special Envoys] Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and the Ukrainian negotiating team, which took place after the meeting between President Trump and Zelenskyy, where perhaps something more practical was discussed," Tsahkna went on.
The meeting between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov bore little fruit, Tsahkna added.
"They were still talking about the same things: That President Trump wants peace and that further meetings would be arranged. And the only major step we know about publicly is that President Putin was invited to attend the G20 summit. /.../ Russian propaganda will certainly take advantage of this opportunity to show that world leaders want to meet him, that he is emerging from the pressure of isolation and that he is an equal among everyone else. And in some ways, that does nothing to help bring peace to Ukraine."
Tsahkna was also critical of the meeting between German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Lavrov.
"We understand that Wadephul raised the issue of the Leipzig attack, but if we look at Russian propaganda, the image presented was essentially one in which Wadephul was very eager to meet. It was a total Russian propaganda victory, I would say, or at least they exploited it to the maximum, and it came across more as a humiliation. Just consider the historical ties between Russia — the successor to the Soviet Union — and Germany. Russia is essentially attacking Germany militarily today, although it is not at the level of Article 5, and then this meeting takes place, after which Lavrov even says, so to speak, that they accommodated the Germans by agreeing to meet and hear them out. And then comes the full-blown propaganda," Tsahkna said.
According to Tsahkna, Russia's top leaders have recently become increasingly amenable as diplomatic interlocutors as well.
"Unfortunately, they are increasingly being treated as acceptable interlocutors, with more and more meetings taking place. But I also had a longer meeting with the Indian foreign minister, who explained that India is currently working very actively to secure an agreement on the Black Sea, particularly on grain exports. And I would also remind you that the Russians sank or fired on ships carrying quite a few Indian sailors. This is something that greatly concerns India. So in that sense, the expansion of the war beyond Ukrainian territory, both into Europe and affecting other countries or citizens connected with other countries, is something that has made many people nervous, particularly the issue of food security and the closure of the Black Sea," Tsahkna continued.
Tsahkna said he had to explain to some colleagues the realities of hybrid warfare versus the credible threat of an actual attack from Russia.
"This is something people are very concerned about, and it also gives us an opportunity to explain that, first of all, we do not see Russia carrying out military maneuvers beyond our borders. However, Russia is using all kinds of hybrid methods, drone attacks, sabotage and terrorist attacks — no longer so much directly against the Baltic states as against Germany and some other large countries. And globally, nobody really likes that. An aggressive Russia is not something anyone likes, and this casts Putin in a bad light, in a new way," Tsahkna said.
"And if you look at the headlines, it seems as though Russia is preparing for war and is about to attack someone in this region. But if you read the intelligence reports or talk to our intelligence people, who have a very good view of what is happening in Russia, they continue to say that the likelihood of preparations for a military invasion or aggression remains extremely low," the minister went on.
"Many different things are being combined, and that only benefits Russia if it creates this atmosphere of fear, this fear of escalation. And that is very characteristic of the Western world: for God's sake, let's not escalate, let's not be the ones to escalate, because otherwise we might end up at war. And that is simply one method of pressure that Putin has been using very skilfully against Western democracies for years," Tsahkna said.
Zelenskyy said during Tuesday's meeting he urged Trump to press Beijing to marshal its influence over Moscow, in order to help bring the invasion to an end.
Washington meanwhile is seeking initial "technical" talks between U,S,, Ukrainian and Russian delegations, with the UAE suggested as a possible venue
Zelenskyy also said Trump had approved the process to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot air defense systems under license.
The Wadephul-Lavrov meeting on Saturday was the first such talks since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russia began in February 2022, and was largely fruitless.

Mapping Israel’s 300 checkpoints: Where they are and how they work
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:50:37 UTC
17:50:37 KST

Mapping Israel’s 300 checkpoints: Where they are and how they work
Israel has shut occupied West Bank crossings for a week, further restricting Palestinian movement and holy site access.
Israel has sealed off the occupied West Bank for a week, shutting its crossings and tightening restrictions on Palestinian movement, citing the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.
Defence Minister Israel Katz on Sunday ordered the closure on the military’s recommendation, and it will remain in place until Saturday.
Palestinians already face severe restrictions on their movement due to hundreds of Israeli checkpoints and barriers across the occupied territory. Now, controls at checkpoints and barriers across the territory will tighten further, cutting off access to holy sites such as the Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem and the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron in the West Bank.
In the Ramallah and el-Bireh governorate on Sunday, Israeli forces blocked roads and shut the entrances to Turmus Aya, Aboud, Nabi Saleh, Atara and Taybeh. In Yabroud, Ein Siniya and Jaba, soldiers set up checkpoints to search vehicles and check IDs.
The closure also bars Palestinians who still hold permits to work in Israel and its settlements, a workforce already sharply reduced since Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza began in October 2023. Only workers deemed essential are allowed into Israeli industrial zones in the West Bank.
How many Palestinians work in Israel?
For decades, Palestinians in the West Bank have looked for work inside Israel because of high unemployment and low wages at home, which are the result of nearly six decades of Israeli occupation that has restricted their economy, land and movement.
The United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution in September 2024 calling on Israel to end its “unlawful” occupation within a year. Israel has since doubled down, intensifying raids on Palestinians, deploying soldiers with settlers during their increasing attacks on Palestinian towns and expanding its settlements, which are illegal under international law.
Before the war on Gaza began, about 160,000 Palestinians from the West Bank worked for Israeli employers, most of them inside Israel and the rest in settlements, according to the Palestinian Institute for Economic Policy Research.
After Israel barred most permit holders from entering, that number fell to about 27,300, by mid-2024. Unemployment in the West Bank rose from 12.9 percent in September 2023 to 30.7 percent a year later, according to the Israeli rights group Gisha.
How many Israeli checkpoints are there?
There are more than 300 Israeli checkpoints across the West Bank, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. As of December, they were among 925 obstacles restricting the movement of 3.4 million Palestinians across the West Bank and East Jerusalem. They are:
- 89 checkpoints staffed 24/7
- 218 partial checkpoints staffed intermittently, 152 of which have gates (90 usually open and 62 frequently closed)
- 232 road gates, 159 of them frequently closed
- 114 linear closures, such as earth walls, road barriers and trenches
- 167 earth mounds
- 105 roadblocks
Where are some of the main checkpoints?
For Palestinians in the West Bank, these checkpoints cut off or restrict access between towns and main roads, forcing hundreds of thousands of people onto longer routes to work and school. They also hinder access to medical care.
Some of the main checkpoints include:
- Qalandiya checkpoint: The main crossing between Ramallah and East Jerusalem once handled about a third of all movement between the West Bank and Israel.
- Checkpoint 300: It blocks the road between Bethlehem and Jerusalem and is the main route for Palestinians working in East Jerusalem and other central cities.
- Eyal checkpoint: It serves workers from Qalqilya, where Israel’s separation wall has driven up unemployment, and from across the northern West Bank.
- Taybeh checkpoint: It lies just south of the northern Palestinian city of Tulkarem.
- Tarqumiyah checkpoint: It is near Hebron in the southern West Bank.

====================================================================================================

King of the Hills: how one man is reshaping the West Bank
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:48:53 UTC
17:48:53 KST

The Palestinian farmhouses scattered across the ridge above Wadi Qana look less like places to rest than small fortresses. Barbed wire surrounds them. Floodlights and cameras rise above the roofs. Metal grilles cover the windows, and heavy gates are bolted shut.
The owners say the fortifications are new, built after a year of repeated incursions, stone-throwing, vandalism and confrontations involving Israelis from newly established hilltop outposts nearby. Farmer Abd al-Rahim Abu Shaib even hung a warning sign in Hebrew outside his home, hoping it might deter intruders. He says hundreds of his olive trees were destroyed.
Until about a year ago, he says, settlers rarely came this close. Then a young man in a white Toyota began driving around the area, asking questions.
Abu Shaib says the man told him he had no future there and should leave for Jordan. Another Palestinian landowner, Fadi Hayek, says the same man threatened him and declared that the land belonged to Jews because God had promised it to them thousands of years ago.
Hayek later pulled up a photograph on his phone. The man, he said, was Elisha Yered.
At 26, Yered has emerged as one of the most prominent organizers and public voices of Israel’s hilltop outpost movement, a network that has expanded rapidly across the West Bank and increasingly into Areas B and A, where under the Oslo Accords the Palestinian Authority exercises civilian control. Recent Israeli reporting has also described Yered as a key organizer of illegal outposts. The Times of Israel
The campaign is not simply a collection of teenagers throwing up tents on remote hillsides. It has logistics, fundraising, communications teams, equipment and a political vision. Yered has become one of its most recognizable faces, publicly promoting a strategy aimed at changing facts on the ground before the Israeli government formally changes the law or abandons the Oslo framework.
A new target on the map
Dozens of unauthorized outposts have been established in Area C during the current government’s term. In the past two years, the report documents at least 23 more in Area B and another in Area A, together covering roughly 100,000 dunams, much of it Palestinian agricultural land. Israeli forces have dismantled some of them, only for activists to return and rebuild after troops leave. Israeli security forces have recently confirmed demolitions of illegal outposts in Area B, underscoring the growing phenomenon. The Times of Israel
The latest focus is an area activists call “Gush Qana,” around Wadi Qana in the northern West Bank. The stated goal is to create a chain of outposts linking Yitzhar and Emmanuel and, in the activists’ own language, interrupt Palestinian territorial continuity between the northern and southern West Bank.
Three outposts have already been established in the area: Mevo Qana, Tzon Aviezer and Kfar Ro’im.
This is not an officially approved Israeli settlement plan. According to the reporting, there was no cabinet decision creating it, no formal planning process and no consultation with security officials. Israel officially removes unauthorized outposts built in Areas A and B, even as activists repeatedly return.
Yered, however, promotes the strategy openly. On WhatsApp, X, Telegram and Facebook, he circulates maps and diagrams showing where activists believe new Jewish footholds should be established. One slogan declares: “Cut the arteries of the Palestinian state, redeem Gush Qana.”
In a regular column in the religious-right magazine Olam Katan, he has outlined what he sees as a broader hilltop strategy, including a list of 10 mountains he considers essential to achieving Israeli sovereignty across the West Bank.
From hilltop youth to movement spokesman
Yered was born in Ramat Gan and moved as a young child with his family to the former settlement of Sa-Nur in the northern West Bank. As a teenager he took part in establishing outposts and was at one point subjected to an administrative order barring him from the territory.
After the last election, he briefly served as spokesman for Otzma Yehudit lawmaker Limor Son Har-Melech before leaving the job. He later became a high-profile figure on social media and an increasingly articulate spokesman for the ideological world known simply as “the hills.”
That ideology rejects the existing legal and political boundaries governing settlement in the West Bank. Its activists view Jewish control of the land as a goal that should be advanced directly, even when government policy has not formally authorized it.
For Yered, Wadi Qana is directly connected to the Oslo Accords.
In an AI-generated video circulated by his movement, he recounts a story about the final negotiations over Oslo II in September 1995, claiming Yasser Arafat insisted on receiving territorial continuity between Nablus and Ramallah. The video argues that the answer, 30 years later, is Jewish control of Wadi Qana.
Whatever the historical dramatization, the political message is explicit: the activists see hilltop outposts as a tool for changing the territorial map created by Oslo.
The machinery behind the hills
The outposts have developed an increasingly organized support system.
The Frontline Hills Administration and the Hills Fund provide logistical and financial assistance, according to their own publications. Their activities include construction materials, furniture, security equipment, sheep, solar systems, water infrastructure, road building, transportation and drones.
Before Rosh Hashanah, Yered published footage showing workers laying a permanent water line to Tzon Aviezer and Kfar Ro’im after months in which residents relied on water tanks and jerrycans.
The Hills Fund said in its annual report that it had supported more than 20 settlement points in Areas A and B and provided guidance to more than 15 new hilltops on selecting “strategic” locations and establishing themselves on the ground.
Fundraising pages solicit donations for specific costs, including 450 shekels to maintain a day of work on a hilltop, 860 shekels for a shepherd’s security kit and 2,000 shekels for a sheep.
The activists insist their operations do not rely on government funding.
Dror Etkes of Kerem Navot, an organization that tracks Israeli settlement activity, questions whether crowdfunding alone can cover the infrastructure visible on the ground. Building kilometers of access roads with heavy machinery, he argues, costs far more than the tens of thousands of shekels raised in individual campaigns.
The Justice Ministry’s public registry, according to the report, shows no government allocations to the registered nonprofits connected to some of the fundraising. Yered himself is not affiliated with those nonprofits, but he is active in the Frontline Hills Administration alongside other prominent hilltop organizers.
Palestinians fear what comes next
For Palestinian farmers living beneath the new outposts, the ideological debate is already tangible.
Abu Shaib says his property has repeatedly been entered and damaged. Hayek says he was threatened. Residents of nearby villages say confrontations and harassment have become part of daily life since the outposts appeared.
In Deir Istiya, southwest of Nablus, residents are now looking toward the olive harvest with anxiety. Village council head Izzat Mansour says locals fear the new hilltop residents will prevent farmers from reaching their groves.
“They don’t want to live with us,” he said. “They want to live here instead of us.”
Dr. Nafis Mansour, who heads the village farmers’ committee, said repeated evacuations followed by the activists’ return have convinced many Palestinians that the state is unwilling or unable to stop the process.
Israeli rights group Yesh Din goes further, arguing that the spread of outposts cannot be separated from the conduct of Israeli authorities and alleging that weak enforcement effectively enables their expansion. That is the organization’s assessment, not an official Israeli government position.
Religious activist Roi Kleitman of Bnei Avraham, a group sharply critical of hilltop extremists, argues that Yered’s influence now extends well beyond the outposts themselves. Through his writing and social media presence, Kleitman says, ideas once confined to the radical margins have entered broader religious-Zionist debate.
That may be Yered’s most significant achievement. The outposts remain unauthorized, security forces still dismantle some of them and the government has not formally adopted his map. But on the hills themselves, new roads are being opened, water pipes laid and structures rebuilt after evacuations.
One man is not literally redrawing the West Bank alone. But Yered has become the clearest face of a movement trying to do exactly that, one hill at a time.

Asian Games | Japan sweeps BMX racing golds as China takes silver, bronze

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28

NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Japan claimed both BMX racing gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, with Sae Hatakeyama winning the women's final and Asuma Nakai retaining his men's title.
China's Lin Haochao edged Indonesia's Fasya Ahsana Rifki by 0.033 seconds to secure men's bronze.
Racing took place in light rain at the Nagoya Velodrome BMX Race Course. Each category featured three preliminary runs, with the top four riders from each heat advancing to an eight-rider final decided over a single race.
Liao finished second in all three of her preliminary runs, while teammate Wang Mengyao won the first two runs in her heat. In the women's final, Hatakeyama crossed the line in 33.401 seconds, with Liao second in 34.500 and Indonesia's Jasmine Azzahra Setyobudi third in 34.932. Wang was relegated to eighth in the official results.
Competing at her first Asian Games, Liao said nerves had affected her since the previous evening and through the preliminaries. In the final, she concentrated on her start, acceleration and the sections ahead.
"I performed above my usual level today," she said, also praising Wang for assisting her through the turns.
The Chinese team had trained in Linyi, Shandong Province, for more than a month but had only three one-hour sessions on the Nagoya course. The rain added another challenge, as Liao had never raced in wet conditions before.
"I'm quite satisfied," Liao said of her silver medal, adding that she hoped the team could build on this performance at next year's Asian championships.
In the men's final, Nakai, the Hangzhou 2022 champion, finished in 30.103 seconds. Fellow Japanese rider Hyoga Kiuchi took silver in 30.583. Lin crossed the line in 32.947, just ahead of Indonesia's Fasya Ahsana Rifki in 32.980. China's Chen Yucheng placed fifth in 33.466.
"I just wanted to give everything and sprint for the line," said Lin, who finished fourth at the previous Asian Games.
Peng Haibo, deputy secretary-general of the Chinese Cycling Association, said the team was satisfied with its performance. China had set out to challenge for women's gold and reach the men's final, and came away with medals in both events.
Peng described the Games as an opportunity to test the team's preparation in a major competition and said riders and coaches would apply the lessons learned as they continue training with an eye on Olympic qualification and the Los Angeles 2028 Games.
BMX racing made its Olympic debut at Beijing 2008 and was introduced to the Asian Games program at Guangzhou 2010. ■

16:47:52 CST
17:47:52 KST

TOKYO, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Damage from raccoons is mounting across Japan as the invasive species expands its habitat from rural areas into cities, Kyodo News reported Monday.
Japanese official data showed that nationwide agricultural crop losses caused by raccoons reached 693 million yen (around 4.4 million U.S. dollars) in fiscal 2024, more than double the amount recorded a decade earlier.
In particular, raccoon damage has become increasingly noticeable in urban areas in recent years. In the western city of Osaka, for example, complaints from residents about raccoons have steadily grown, from 161 in fiscal 2023 to 332 in fiscal 2024 and 397 in fiscal 2025, the report said.
Among the complaints were reports of goldfish being eaten from garden ponds and the animals breaking into attics.
Raccoons also ranked first among wildlife species causing agricultural damage in Osaka Prefecture, accounting for over 40 percent of the total, with crop losses of 84.06 million yen in fiscal 2024, twice the amount recorded the previous year.
Osaka prefectural authorities believe the animals are settling in residential areas in search of food and have urged residents not to approach or feed them.
More places where raccoons can breed, such as vacant houses, may have also helped expand their habitat, the report said, citing an official from the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
Hokkaido in the north is facing a similar problem, with raccoons spreading to nearly the entire prefecture by the end of January this year.
Local officials said raccoon numbers are increasing so quickly that it has become an endless battle.
Nevertheless, experts said continued efforts, such as setting traps, are needed to reduce the animal's population and limit the damage they cause. ■

Skyranger Air Defense System to Receive Rheinmetall’s Automatic Reloading System
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:47:52 UTC
17:47:52 KST

Rheinmetall is developing a dedicated vehicle for the automatic reloading of Skyranger SAM systems.
Militär Aktuell reported this.
The new vehicle is intended to reduce ammunition replenishment time and let crews stay inside the protected vehicles during reloading.
Rheinmetall is developing the project in cooperation with Austrian partners and the country’s Armed Forces.
Austrian companies Empl and Palfinger, which specialize in specialized transport vehicles and lifting equipment, are involved in the development. The project is currently in the development stage, and Rheinmetall has not yet received an order for series production of the system.
According to the developers, the dedicated vehicle will load a prepared ammunition magazine into the combat vehicle using a robotic manipulator.
It will remove the empty magazine, replace it with a full one, and return for the next one.
Each magazine contains 252 rounds and weighs approximately 400 kg. Rheinmetall expects the entire reloading process to take only a few minutes.
Austria has ordered 36 Skyranger 30 systems mounted on Pandur EVO armored personnel carrier chassis. The new reloading system is intended to extend the systems’ operating time without requiring crews to carry out dangerous operations outside the vehicle.
In addition to the dedicated reloading vehicle, Rheinmetall is considering using a trailer carrying additional magazines. It could carry up to 12 magazines, while the reloading vehicle itself would carry six. This would give the system up to 18 additional magazines, or around 4,500 rounds.
It is currently being developed primarily for the Skyranger 30 system, but the solution is planned for adaptation to the Skyranger 35 in the future.
The module is equipped with a Swiss 30 mm Oerlikon KCE cannon with a fire rate of 1,200 rounds per minute. Optionally, it can be fitted with a launcher for two FIM-92 Stinger or Mistral missiles.
The cannon’s ammunition suite includes a wide range of rounds, including proximity-fuzed shells. The ammunition load consists of 252 30 mm rounds.
For detecting small aerial targets, the Skyranger 30 also uses the AMMR multi-mission radar, which operates in the S-band. A total of five antennas are installed on the vehicle, providing 360-degree coverage.
The countries that have placed orders include Denmark, Hungary, and the Netherlands. All three countries will mount the Skyranger module on their own platforms.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Election Commission to decide the dispute between two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) over the party's name and its “flowers and grass” election symbol within three months.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked both factions to complete their pleadings before the poll panel within four weeks.The court directed the Election Commission to take a final decision on the dispute within three months after the completion of pleadings by both sides.The court passed the order while hearing a plea filed by former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee challenging the EC’s decision to freeze the TMC’s name and “flowers and grass” election symbol.The development comes days after the Election Commission temporarily allotted Mamata Banerjee’s faction the name “Mamata All India Trinamool Congress” and the “football player” symbol. The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both factions have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the poll panel after rival groups staked claims to control the TMC. The Commission subsequently sought submissions on issues including organisational control, authorised office-bearers, party assets, the party name and its election symbol.

Hristina Hranova: a Bulgarian woman who devoted herself to her homeland
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:47:33 UTC
17:47:33 KST

Author
Diana Tsankova
Article
Hristina Hranova: a Bulgarian woman who devoted herself to her homeland
The young woman fought in more than one war of liberation and became Bulgaria’s first qualified midwife and its first female lifeguard
Monday 28 September 2026 10:12
Monday, 28 September 2026, 10:12
Hristina Hranova (1852-1922)
PHOTO Regional Library "Pencho Slaveykov" - Varna
Font size
For Bulgarians living under Ottoman rule, the "Fatherland” embodied the yearning for freedom. Yet the struggle for that freedom demanded more than a self-sacrificing martial spirit. It called for an ascent along a path whose highest ideals included the relentless pursuit of self-improvement and selfless service to others. There were indeed men and women who recognised the historic moment and forged within themselves the qualities that would lead them to deeds worthy of remembrance. Among them was Hristina Hranova.
I carried letters, disguised as a man, for the First Sofia, Fourth Panagyurishte and Eighth Lovech revolutionary committees, acting on the orders and instructions of the great Levski, through forests and mountains, day and night, in fair weather and foul weather. On the day of the terrible massacre in Batak, I found myself inside the very church where so many innocent people perished, and I escaped only by a miracle. When the hour of Liberation came, I fought with a weapon in my hands alongside the glorious Bulgarian volunteers at Shipka, Sheinovo and Stara Zagora…
PHOTO europeana.eu
Hristina Hranova was born in 1852 in the village of Klisura in the family od Hrano Tsenkov, the shepherd - as she was the youngest of twelve brothers and five sisters. At the age of twelve, she shot the leader of a Turkish bashi-bazouk band who had attempted to slay her mother with a sabre. Her father then loaded his large family onto a cart and took them to Sofia.
The young girl received her education at the school founded by Yordanka Filaretova, and when the opportunity arose for her to assist the Apostle of Freedom Vasil Levski, she did not hesitate.
Hristina Hranova, Vasil Levski
PHOTO europeana.eu, museumvt.com
At the age of 18, Hristina became a courier for the Sofia Revolutionary Committee on Levski’s recommendation, Magdalena Gigova recounts in her “Addresses of Love” series on BNR’s Radio Sofia.
“Every week, mounted on her horse and disguised as a boy, she travelled between Sofia, Lovech and Panagyurishte, carrying Levski’s letters. Their relationship apparently transcended the formal tone of their correspondence, and thoughts of the fair-haired young hero remained with her throughout her life, preserved as something pure and untouched. Before long, terrible news reached the Hranov family: Levski had been captured and sentenced to death. Hristina disguised herself as a shepherdess, draped a *yamurluk* over her shoulders, took a shepherd’s crook in her hand and went near the place of execution to see the Apostle of Freedom one last time. When he was hanged, an even fiercer determination to avenge the precious sacrifice took hold of her. She witnessed the hanging of the Deacon, as Levski was also called, and in her writings referred to him as ‘the Great One’.”
During the April Uprising of 1876, Hristina Hranova took part in the fighting at Batak. A year later, she joined the Bulgarian volunteer corps as a nurse and passed through the crucible of the battles at Shipka, Sheinovo and Stara Zagora. In the meantime, ten of her brothers lost their lives as volunteers in the Serbo-Turkish War and the Russo-Turkish War.
Hristina Hranova, sitting on the right as a student at the Midwifery Institute of the Imperial St. Vladimir University in Kyiv
PHOTO europeana.eu
Having fulfilled my sacred duty to the Fatherland, believing that in times of hardship a woman can serve her homeland on an equal footing with a man, I set out to study. I became a midwife and, in this capacity, for many years helped thousands of mothers bring thousands of brave sons and worthy daughters into the world. By my own hand, I helped no fewer than 3,462 lives emerge from the wombs of women in labour. During those years, among other things, I saved at least 54 people from certain death by drowning, whether through carelessness or accident, in the waves of the Black Sea during the various bathing seasons…
Imperial St. Vladimir University in Kyiv
PHOTO europeana.eu
Having witnessed the freedom she had fought for, Hristina Hranova travelled to Kyiv, where, with the help of a scholarship awarded to talented students, she graduated with distinction from the Midwifery Institute of St. Vladimir Imperial University, becoming the first qualified midwife in Bulgaria. Thanks to her dedicated work, the first maternity ward in Sofia was established. She practised her noble profession in several Bulgarian cities, including Varna.
It was also in Varna, in the Armenian Quarter, where she taught children to read and write and, in summer, to swim. It was in the seaside city that she became not only Bulgaria’s first female lifeguard, but reportedly the first woman to serve in that capacity in the world.
PHOTO Regional Library "Pencho Slaveykov" - Varna
“She was such a strong swimmer that in 1908, in those decidedly male-dominated times when women would venture no further than ankle-deep into the water, fully clothed from head to toe, she swam the five-kilometre distance from Varna to Cape Galata at the age of 56,” Magdalena Gigova continues. “She was probably also Bulgaria’s first unofficial female competitive swimmer. It was said of her: ‘When wagers were made on long-distance swimming, she would defeat young sailors despite her age.’ She also had a playful sense of humour. On one occasion, disguised as a black sea monster, she suddenly emerged from the water near the men’s bathing area, sending around a hundred frightened men running for safety.”
But when, following the Unification, the Serbs threatened the freedom of the Fatherland, I could not remain still. I seized my rifle and went to the border, where, as a volunteer, I took an active part in the battles at Dragoman, Gurgulyat and Slivnitsa…
Serbo-Bulgarian War
PHOTO wellcomecollection.org
Although deeply devoted to her profession, the call of the homeland proved stronger
"During the Serbo-Bulgarian War of 1885, Hristina Hranova was once again a heroine, and this time she was wounded in the left knee,” Magdalena Gigova says. “She not only wielded a weapon, but also carried medicines in her bag and tended to the sick and wounded. People began to call her, gratefully, ‘Mother of the Heroes’. Nearly 30 years after the Russo-Turkish War of Liberation, Hristina donned a soldier’s uniform for the last time and enlisted as a volunteer, this time in the Second Balkan War of 1913. She was around 60 at the time and later admitted that she had overestimated her strength. She took part in the fighting at Kumanovo, Kriva Palanka, Kochani and Dzhumaya.”
Old, frail and infirm, I am no longer able to earn my livelihood, and my last remaining strength is slowly ebbing away in this terrible misery. There are days when I am forced to go hungry. In winter, I shiver from the cold. I ask for little; help me only so that I may not die of hunger and cold. Mercy, mercy, sons of Bulgaria…
Years later, she would pose for a postcard in a ceremonial military uniform, wearing a Bulgarian volunteer’s tunic and six orders and medals on her chest. Yet the hardships of life did not spare her. She discovered that winning a battle against bureaucratic indifference could be more difficult than prevailing on the battlefield. In 1910, she was denied a state pension on the grounds that she had not made regular social security contributions.
PHOTO europeana.eu
“Hristina found little joy in her personal life and remained alone to the end, never marrying,” Magdalena Gigova says in conclusion. “Her self-assurance must have intimidated men. What kind of husband would a woman who kept a rifle in her bedroom have? She lived quietly, almost unnoticed, while her health steadily deteriorated. ‘And here I am today, a ruin,’ she would write. Until the end of her days, she was crippled by rheumatoid arthritis. She lived in a wooden shack and was forced to spend her days on the street, holding out her hand for a crust of bread. She languished in extreme poverty, often going hungry for days at a time. Despite her honours and her service to the state, it took nearly eight years for her petitions for a pension to receive a response. In 1918, the National Assembly granted her a lifelong state pension of 60 leva, barely enough to keep her from starvation.”
In 1922,  after years of suffering and hardship, Hristina Hranova died passed away.at the age of 72.
“She was not buried with military honours, and only her old comrades-in-arms accompanied her on her final journey. The location of her grave remains unknown. ‘A grave without a monument, a grave long since erased,’ writes her biographer Kiril Bozhilov. Despite her exploits and achievements, despite the lives she helped bring into the world and those she saved, the life and legacy of Hristina Hranova have remained outside the pantheon of great Bulgarians, without an epitaph, a cross or a monument. In Varna, where she worked as a midwife and lifeguard, there is a street named after her. Yet although the postcard issued in her honour as a commemorative keepsake bears the inscription ‘From Sofia’, with the word ‘native’ in brackets, the capital has yet to pay tribute to her. Let us honour in our thoughts this remarkable woman, Hristina Hranova!” Magdalena Gigova concludes.
Text: Diana Tsankova, based on a feature by Magdalena Gigova, broadcast on BNR’s Radio Sofia
Editor: D. Semkovska
English version: R. Petkova

Feature: Shanghai brings Chinese rhythms to Barcelona's La Merce
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
16:47:22 CST
17:47:22 KST

BARCELONA, Spain, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Music flowed into squares, dancers and street performers filled public spaces, and fireworks lit up Barcelona's waterfront as the city celebrated La Merce, one of its most important annual festivals, from Sept. 23 to 27.
This year, the familiar festival rhythm carried a distinctive Chinese note. As 2026 marks the 25th anniversary of the sister-city relationship between Shanghai and Barcelona, Shanghai became the first Asian city to serve as La Merce's guest city. More than 100 artists delivered 14 performances spanning acrobatics, dance, jazz, and traditional Chinese music.
The Fengxian rolling lantern performance was among the opening-night highlights. After traditional Catalan giant figures performed at Sant Jaume Square on Sept. 23, artists from Shanghai's Fengxian District took the stage with large golden lanterns, lifting and rolling them through a series of demanding moves. Near the end, sparks burst from the lanterns, echoing an earlier traditional Catalan dragon that sprayed sparks into the night and drawing cheers from thousands of spectators.
Esteve Carames, director of cultural programs at the Barcelona Institute of Culture, said the Fengxian rolling lanterns were chosen for the opening ceremony because of their distinctive regional character and connection with coastal life.
"Barcelona is also a coastal city," he told Xinhua. "We blended Barcelona's distinctive traditions with those of Shanghai."
Similar cross-cultural touches ran through Shanghai's guest-city program.
Later that evening, at Doctor Pla i Armengol Gardens, the Shanghai Conservatory of Music Jazz Ensemble incorporated the suona, a traditional Chinese wind instrument, into contemporary jazz arrangements. Its bright, piercing sound mingled with trumpet and percussion as audience members danced along.
Two nights later at Barcelona's Cathedral Square, the Shanghai Chinese Orchestra presented the AI-composed concert "Zero/One: Colors of China," featuring Shanghai-style traditional music as well as an adaptation of the Spanish flamenco work "Gitana Hechicera."
"One of the most attractive things about Shanghai is the way tradition is combined with highly innovative projects, and that is very similar to Barcelona's understanding of culture," Carames said.
That cultural dialogue was also visible onstage.
Castells, or human towers, are among Catalonia's best-known folk traditions, with participants climbing onto one another's shoulders to build towers several levels high.
Echoing that tradition, the Fengxian performers added a "stacked rolling lantern" sequence, lifting the lanterns layer by layer.
Beyond the stage, the program invited local residents to take part.
At Estacio del Nord Park, a Chinese games corner organized by the Confucius Institute Foundation of Barcelona drew more than 6,000 participants. Visitors learned Chinese numbers and simple greetings through games and joined handicraft activities.
Wang Jinwei, co-director of the Confucius Institute Foundation of Barcelona, said such activities had no clear boundary between performers and spectators, allowing children and parents to experience Chinese culture through play.
After a performance by the Shanghai Dance School in the same park, one Barcelona resident asked a Xinhua reporter whether there would be another show. "I want to come back during the holiday and bring my family with me," he said.
The Chinese presence also took to the sky.
On Sept. 24, 750 drones rose into the night sky above the Barceloneta waterfront to mark the 25th anniversary of the sister-city relationship. The drones formed images including the Monkey King and the Oriental Pearl Tower alongside familiar Barcelona landmarks such as the Sagrada Familia.
Tens of thousands of residents and tourists gathered along the waterfront, cheering as new images took shape in the sky.
Videos of the drone show later spread across Chinese social media. On Xiaohongshu, a video captioned "Seeing Shanghai's skyline in Barcelona" drew thousands of likes and comments. One Shanghai user wrote: "Wishing my family in Barcelona good health and all the best." The video was posted on the Mid-Autumn Festival, a traditional occasion for family reunions in China.
Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni said at the opening ceremony that the 25-year relationship between Barcelona and Shanghai is not only a link between municipal governments, but also a human bond built day by day by Barcelona's Chinese community.
Xavier Marce, Barcelona city councilor for culture and creative industries, said the events had opened a door to further exchanges.
"This is only the beginning," he said. "We are very confident that, taking this event in Barcelona as a starting point, there will be more exchanges and cooperation between Barcelona and Shanghai in the coming years." ■

UK security forces were aware of RAF Fairford suspected bomb plot, hints defence secretary
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
08:47:15 UTC
17:47:15 KST

UK security services were aware in advance about a group of men arrested in connection with a suspected bomb plot against an RAF base used by the US military, Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, has indicated.
Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences after armed officers found explosives in three vans parked minutes from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, from which the US air force flies missions against Iran.
Police were alerted after a local woman driving near the base in the early hours of Sunday saw the vans and men acting unusually and called 999. Speaking to the BBC on Monday morning, the woman said security services had seemingly “really dropped the ball on this”.
Speaking later to BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, Streeting said that while he wanted to thank the woman – who has chosen to remain anonymous – for calling police, she had “a partial picture”.
He praised police and security services for their work, referencing comments by Donald Trump who claimed the suspects had been under view for a long time.
Trump alleged the men “were looking to do big damage” and said of the response: “It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job.”
Streeting, when asked if he was saying Trump had been correct, did not reject this. “Our security services and our police, they don’t ask for praise, but I think it was a proud moment yesterday to see the president of the United States recognise the extraordinary work that our police and our security and intelligence services do every day throughout the year and throughout the world to keep us safe. That’s all I want to say this morning on that,” he said.
It is understood that UK officials believe there is no contradiction between Trump’s comments that the men were being watched and the fact that an alert was made to police by a member of the public, indicating that they were likely to have been intercepted anyway.
Streeting declined to give any details about any prior information about the suspected plot or the identities of the men arrested.
He said: “There’s a live police investigation, and as a matter of course we don’t comment in detail on operational security matters, because often the more that we might say, the more insight we give to those who would wish us harm and do us harm, given the opportunity.”
Images showed shirtless men being handcuffed in a dark country lane after police were called to reports of three suspicious vans travelling towards RAF Fairford.
During the major incident, the residents of 85 households in the Cotswolds village of Whelford were rapidly evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre and a 400-metre cordon was placed around the white vans as robots from the army’s bomb squad examined them.
In comments read out by a member of BBC staff, the local woman who called the police said she had been driving home late from a party but that when she reached her farm she found the driveway and the road blocked by three white vans.
Thinking this was related to security operations at RAF Fairford, she turned her car around, but then she saw a group of men wearing hoods and masks, who she said ran away when they saw her. Suspicious, she called Ministry of Defence police and then 999.
She said: “I think it was pure luck that I arrived in the village at a similar time to the vans. I am absolutely staggered that it was left to me, as a member of the public, to see and report this.
“The airbase were operating a roadblock close to the entrance to the base, but not on any of the other roads. But we assumed someone would be monitoring the roads around the base perimeter and taking regular patrols in the village.”
She said: “I’m just really keen to highlight that it appears someone really dropped the ball on this.”

Ukraine Flies 4 Tons of Food by Drone Into Occupied Oleshky, Reaching 100 Locations

Ukraine Flies 4 Tons of Food by Drone Into Occupied Oleshky, Reaching 100 Locations
Ukraine is using drones to move humanitarian supplies across the Dnipro River into temporarily occupied Oleshky, where conventional aid deliveries remain severely restricted.
Ukrainian forces have delivered approximately four tons of food by drone to civilians in the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region, distributing supplies across 100 locations as conventional humanitarian access remains restricted.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Kherson Regional Governor Oleksandr Prokudin on September 27, Ukrainian units have been transporting food across the Dnipro River by unmanned aerial vehicles since March.
One of the largest such operations was carried out recently with the participation of Ukraine’s 30th Marine Corps, the Hrim tactical group, the 34th Borysfen Marine Brigade, the Bolharychi unit of the 11th National Guard Brigade, the 34th National Guard Regiment, and the 79th Border Guard Detachment.
The units delivered around 4,000 kilograms of food to 100 designated locations across Oleshky, Prokudin said.
He also said Russian forces have attempted to disrupt the deliveries by shooting down drones carrying humanitarian supplies and confiscating or reselling food intended for local residents. According to Prokudin, residents have also faced detention and physical abuse for receiving the packages.
Oleshky, located on the temporarily occupied left bank of the Dnipro River, has faced worsening shortages of food, medicine, electricity, and transportation.
Regular food deliveries to the area stopped at the end of May 2026. More than 6,000 civilians, including approximately 200 children, may remain in Oleshky and nearby settlements close to the front line.
The drone deliveries come as Russia continues to deny humanitarian organizations, including the United Nations, safe access to temporarily occupied Oleshky. The city has been largely cut off from regular food supplies, medicine, electricity, and transport, while evacuation efforts remain stalled due to the lack of security guarantees from Russia.

Russia Buries Three Tanks 65 Km Behind Front Line—Ukrainian Drones Dig Them Up
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

17:45:35 KST

- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russia Buries Three Tanks 65 Km Behind Front Line—Ukrainian Drones Dig Them Up
Ukrainian National Guard drone operators destroyed three Russian tanks concealed about 65 kilometers (40 miles) behind the front line in the Oleksandrivka sector, striking the vehicles despite efforts to protect them with dug-in positions and anti-drone shelters.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The operation was carried out by Lasar’s Group, a drone unit of Ukraine’s National Guard, which released footage of the strikes on its official Facebook page on September 27.
Russian forces had positioned the tanks well away from the immediate front line, partially burying the vehicles and constructing protective structures above them to reduce their exposure to drone attacks.
Lasar’s Group said information about the concentration of armored vehicles was initially provided by aerial reconnaissance teams from neighboring Ukrainian units. Its analysts then verified the location before strike drones were dispatched to the area.
The drones traveled approximately 65 kilometers into Russian-held positions and struck the three tanks one after another, according to the unit. Lasar’s Group said all three vehicles were destroyed before Russian forces were able to deploy them in combat.
The unit said Russian tanks have become less common near the front and claimed its crews have destroyed more than 2,400 Russian tanks since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.
“We can now destroy more tanks on our own than the Russians produce,” Lasar’s Group said.
Ukrainian drone units have also targeted Russian troops elsewhere on the Lyman front. On September 21, Signum released footage showing its operators striking Russian infantry, including troops moving on motorcycles.

Police probe ‘terror’ incident near RAF base used in Iran war: What we know
Five men were arrested on suspicion of the ‘preparation of a terrorist act’ near RAF Fairford, a base used by the US.
British security officials are exploring “multiple lines of enquiry” following the arrest of five men on Sunday morning on suspicion of the “preparation of a terrorist act” near a British Royal Air Force (RAF) base in southern England that has been used by the United States in various conflicts.
Armed officers arrested the group of men after calls from residents to emergency services reported three “suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base”, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement.
